definitions.frame_health_rule: Configured frame HP rule, not total combined health or a universal damage-to-kill threshold.
definitions.health: Configured HP from matching balancing tag rules. Null means no unambiguous match was recovered; it does not mean zero HP.
definitions.health_rules: Complete standard enemy balancing rules, including rules without a match in the linked mesh map. Rule ids are local to that enemy.
definitions.part_query: Gameplay tag expression. ID/Group/HealthGroup abbreviate Part.Decorator. ALL/ANY/NONE preserve the original matching logic.
definitions.resistance_group: Context label only. Every part's damage_response contains its numeric resistance and damage factors directly.
definitions.high_health_values: Large or zero values are preserved as stored. Do not interpret every rule as a practical breakable part or infer invulnerability from the number alone.
definitions.damage_response: Inline resistance and baseline incoming damage multipliers by damage channel. Physical flags specify which separate weapon multiplier applies. Both explosive flag states are numeric; the live flag state is unknown.
definitions.health_assignment_rules: The exact matching HP rules repeated directly on this part, including numeric HP and provenance, so rule ids do not have to be looked up.
definitions.health_and_destruction_settings: Recovered actor overrides, including numeric health thresholds, destruction damage and expanded tag queries. These settings are not a complete simulation of health propagation.
definitions.unassigned_resistance: Null values indicate no serialized resistance assignment recovered for this record. A generic default is not silently assigned to sockets, visual or proxy records.

limits: Standard user-facing profiles only; archived, test and event variants are excluded. Static tag matches do not simulate destruction chains, health-group aggregation or server-side overrides. Some actor/style JSONs were partially decoded; the health tables themselves parsed without those warnings.

damage_model.scope: One part's direct damage stage, before downstream health propagation or destruction chains. Distance, radial exposure, global damage modifiers, and skill modifiers are separate inputs.

formulas.distance_and_area: Multiply the direct stage by the weapon distance factor and the attack's affected-degree/exposure factor. A spherical target routine already includes radial falloff in its affected degree; do not apply that radial curve twice.

explosive_feature_flag.name: constructable_explosive_damage_squish
explosive_feature_flag.reason: The cache calls the runtime feature-flag service. Its active server/session value is not present in this offline dataset. Both numeric branches are included on every assigned part.

unmapped_resistance_type_fallback.meaning: GetResistanceForType returns this for a resistance-type enum outside the five supported channels. This does not assign a group to an unclassified mesh record.

notes: Resistance 0.6 means a baseline 0.4x damage factor; resistance -0.5 means 1.5x damage. Negative resistance is vulnerability.
Armor and Sturdy share baseline resistance but only Armor receives the physical weapon ARC-armour multiplier.
The firearm critical/headshot multiplier is not automatically applied to the ARC Critical resistance group. ARC weak/critical parts use the separate ARC weakpoint multiplier in this calculation.
Weapon ARC-armour and weakpoint multipliers are applied by the recovered physical damage branch, not to explosive/thermal/electric effect magnitudes by this branch.
Armor propagation multipliers describe another stage; the direct numbers here are not automatically frame-health damage or total damage-to-kill.

A part without a serialized resistance-group assignment retains null numeric values. Several such records are sockets, muzzle bones, or visual/proxy components; their group is not guessed from their name or health tags.
